Man Pulls Off Heist, Buys New Dodge Challenger Hellcat From Nebraska Dealer for $17,386 Under MSRP
19 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
If you're in the market for a still-new Hellcat-powered Challenger, I think I may have found one of the best deals out there in this TorRed model. Sadly, it's already been sold, but there's nothing stopping you from trying to find another one just like it.
This car was purchased new by the selling dealer at Baxter Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram in Omaha, Nebraska, for $100,886. That dealer then sold the car at auction for just $83,500 (plus a buyer's fee), but here's the kicker - the odometer read 105 miles. In other words, this thing is still brand spanking new.
As far as I'm concerned, 105 miles is delivery miles. It means the car was moved around a bit from one place to another, probably gassed up, cleaned and so on. This is a new Hellcat for $17,386 below MSRP. It's peak muscle car. I really don't know what more you could want from a Challenger. And don't get me started on the Demon 170 or even the Super Stock. You don't need anything more than a Redeye Jailbreak.
I could argue that you don't need anything more than a base Hellcat , but given where we are today with so many new performance cars hovering around that 1,000 horsepower mark, perhaps 707/717 horsepower might sound a bit "old school", even though it's not. It just goes to show how ridiculous things have gotten on that front. Seems like it was just yesterday that you had to spend millions on a hypercar in order to have over 700 hp.
Anyway, let's take a closer look at the spec on this Challenger, starting with the visuals.
Aside from the TorRed colorway , the car also boasts dual Carbon stripes, a Satin Black SRT Performance spoiler, Brass Monkey badges, HID Air-Catcher headlights, widebody fenders as part of the Widebody package, Redeye badging, a chin spoiler guard, black hood pins, plus a set of 20" Brass Monkey Devil Rim forged wheels with Pirelli P Zero rubber and yellow-finished Brembo calipers. You also get the Widebody competition suspension system with adaptive Bilstein dampers.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the Demonic Red Laguna leather seats (heated/ventilated), a rear seat delete, Copper weave carbon fiber trim, a suede headliner, Demonic Red seatbets, an 18-speaker Harman Kardon sound system, and a heated and Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel.
As for performance, here's what's great about this particular spec. Normally, the supercharged high-output 6.2-liter HEMI V8 would have been putting down 797 horsepower and 707 lb-ft of torque. However, thanks to the Jailbreak package , this Challenger is currently hammering out 807 horsepower. Everything gets sent to the rear wheels via an eight-speed TorqueFlite automatic gearbox and a limited slip differential.
But what do you guys think? Would you have spent $83,500 (plus a buyer's fee) on this Hellcat? Sound off below.
